Long-term ecological monitoring of Nueces Bay seagrass beds and oyster reef habitats will continue under a separate TCEQ Natural Resource Damage Assessment agreement with the owners of MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay Total documented cleanup cost is $8.2 million. Wildlife rehabilitation costs of $0.9 million and estimated commercial fishing economic losses of $5.6 million are subject to Natural Resource Damage Assessment proceedings. This assessment has been transmitted to NOAA, USFWS, and Texas Parks and Wildlife for NRD purposes.

The claims center run for the tankers' owners begins taking lost-income claims from fishers and shoreline businesses, as federal oil spill law requires; claims unpaid after 90 days can go to the Coast Guard's National Pollution Funds Center.
Some aid applicants say their direct-deposit details were changed without their knowledge.
FEMA confirms unauthorized access to some applicant accounts and urges applicants to verify deposit information.
FEMA says 410 accounts were taken over after about 220,000 automated login attempts using passwords stolen elsewhere; extra verification added; affected applicants will be repaid.
A second wave of posts claims contractors are stealing aid; fact-checkers say some contract questions are legitimate but specific posts are false.
Navy suspends Quellmar Fuel Partners pending a fuel quality review linked to the station's generator failure; the company says its fuel meets specifications.
Records show Vantorra Restoration billed for about 2.3 times the debris tonnage the county's own drone and satellite surveys estimated; the company denies overbilling.
County pauses payments to Vantorra pending an audit.
A federal inspector general opens a review of emergency debris and fuel contracts in the Coastal Bend.

Analysis by Coastline Public Radio and a Texas A&M-Corpus Christi researcher: low-income neighborhoods in the surge zone received aid dollars at about half their share of residents, and their median 911 response time was 2.1 times that of high-income areas.

facts.source: FBI Houston Division / Texas Department of Public Safety
facts.statement: OPERATION SANDBAR — 14 ARRESTED IN HURRICANE RAFAEL DISASTER FRAUD SCHEME — December 13, 2027: The Federal Bureau of Investigation Houston Division, FBI Corpus Christi Resident Agency, and the Texas Department of Public Safety Criminal Investigations Division today announced 14 arrests in connection with a large-scale disaster fraud scheme that targeted federal disaster assistance programs and private insurers following Hurricane Rafael. The defendants, led by Corpus Christi resident Renaldo Carver-Mossbach, 44, are accused of fraudulently inflating insurance values on 230 properties before the storm and subsequently filing 187 fraudulent insurance claims and 94 fraudulent FEMA Individual Assistance applications claiming damage that did not occur or was dramatically overstated. Total alleged fraud losses exceed $23 million. Property management company Landmark Pacific Holdings LLC, water damage restoration firm FastDry Coastal LLC, and appraisal firm Duvall and Sons Property Consultants are named in the complaint. The defendants face federal charges of wire fraud, mail fraud, false statements to a federal agency, and conspiracy, carrying maximum penalties of 20 to 30 years in federal prison. FEMA has suspended 94 Individual Assistance awards pending investigation and is contacting affected applicants whose claims were filed without their knowledge. Texas DPS urges any resident who engaged with FastDry Coastal LLC or Landmark Pacific Holdings representatives after the storm to contact the Operation Sandbar tip line at (361) 555-0199.
County and FEMA announce door-to-door aid registration in low-income surge-zone neighborhoods.
Navy orders a security review at Texas air stations after the storm, citing drone reports and the channel attack.
FBI agents execute search warrants Monday, Dec. 27, at the offices of Vantorra Restoration and Quellmar Fuel Partners.
Coast Guard and CISA issue a maritime cyber advisory urging vessel operators to review vendor remote access to cargo systems.
City plans to harden the water plant's power feeds; state reviews bridge wind-closure procedures.
US officials attribute the tanker cyber intrusion and the explosive devices in the ship channel to a foreign government they did not name, calling them attempts to exploit the hurricane.

Federal civil forfeiture filing says Vantorra Restoration and Quellmar Fuel Partners share an owner, Brannoch Maritime Holdings, an offshore company whose listed director is L. Marrick, and that bank accounts tied to the firms received about $3.9 million in diverted disaster aid.
About 4,200 spill damage claims filed; fishing grounds partly reopen after testing.
Four months after Rafael: rebuilding continues; reviews of water, aid equity, port security and contracting are under way.

never_public.description: KESTREL attribution: IP overlap between GW-SYS-JMP-01 session logs and KESTREL C2 infrastructure documented in classified FBI/CISA indicator set. Links the utility attack to Rafael T6/T7 (STATE-X dark network). Classification: TLP:RED.

GW-ENG-VELA credential theft: the specific phishing email, the implant on GW-WS-IT-04, and the full session log export from GW-SYS-JMP-01 are law-enforcement sensitive and not released publicly during the scenario window.
Relay modification details: the specific 27-UV threshold values modified on GW-SYS-RTU-01 through RTU-04 are withheld from public advisories to prevent adversary confirmation of success.

known_quirks: The tanker valves opened about 11 p.m. local on Sept. 13 (04:00Z on landfall day); public wording is 'as the storm arrived'.
FEMA Individual Assistance arrives on day 57-60 because household damage assessments were slowed (PUB-103 to PUB-105); earlier aid came through the disaster declaration, shelters and community hubs.

Two boil-water notices overlap. Citywide: Sept. 18 (day 4) to Oct. 23 (day 39). Districts 3 and 4: issued in English at 5:30 p.m. on Sept. 26 (day 12), reached KNCB in Spanish at 6:03 a.m. on Sept. 27, lifted at 11 a.m. on Oct. 26 (day 42). There was no partial lift on day 30.
There is one oil spill: about 9,000 barrels from MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay at the Rendal Terminals berth. No other vessel was detained or named as a source.
The ship channel is closed from landfall to a partial reopening on day 30, closed again from the blast on day 44, and reopened on day 58. There was no phased reopening before day 30.
911: about 2,900 calls on Sept. 15 (day 1) is the peak; 2,109 on Sept. 16 (day 2) is the record for rescue requests.
FEMA: before Individual Assistance is approved (day 57; registration opens day 60) the FEMA phone number is an information line only.
